  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header of the maamar, including the date and Torah portion.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Vayishlach,</t>
    <t s="2">18 Kislev 5740*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the Gemara's statement that the purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, citing Rashi's interpretation that this refers to the essence of Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"A saying that is regularly in the mouth of Rava: The purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, as it is said,</t>
    <t s="1">'The beginning of wisdom is fear of the L-rd; good understanding to all who do them,'</t>
    <t s="2">It does not say 'to those who study them,' but rather 'to those who do them.'</t>
    <t s="3">And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings this in his maamar beginning "Zeh she'amar" of Shabbos Parshas Vayishlach 5689</t>
    <t s="4">(printed in the Kuntres of Wedding Discourses 5689)</t>
    <t s="5">[with] Rashi's commentary,</t>
    <t s="6">that wisdom is Torah,</t>
    <t s="7">and the purpose of wisdom,</t>
    <t s="8">the essence of Torah,</t>
    <t s="9">is that it should be accompanied by repentance and good deeds.</t>
    <t s="10">And the maamar clarifies,</t>
    <t s="11">that the essence of Torah is understanding and comprehension,</t>
    <t s="12">that one should understand and comprehend what one studies</t>
    <t s="13">[and particularly in the Oral Torah,</t>
    <t s="14">for when one does not understand what one studies, it is not considered study at all],</t>
    <t s="15">and in this statement of our Sages, it says that the essence of Torah is repentance and good deeds.</t>
    <t s="16">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="17">that the reason the maamar brings Rashi's commentary on "the purpose of wisdom,"</t>
    <t s="18">is,</t>
    <t s="19">because the meaning of "purpose" in most places is the ultimate intention,</t>
    <t s="20">and the like.</t>
    <t s="21">And accordingly,</t>
    <t s="22">the meaning of "the purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds" is,</t>
    <t s="23">that the ultimate intention in the study of Torah</t>
    <t s="24">(wisdom)</t>
    <t s="25">is that it should lead to repentance and good deeds.</t>
    <t s="26">Therefore the maamar brings Rashi's commentary that "the purpose of wisdom" is "the essence of Torah."</t>
    <t s="27">For in addition to the fact that the intention of Torah study is that it should lead to repentance and good deeds,</t>
    <t s="28">also the very essence of Torah itself</t>
    <t s="29">[and moreover, its primary essence]</t>
    <t s="30">is repentance and good deeds.</t>
    <t s="31">And therefore it clarifies,</t>
    <t s="32">that wisdom</t>
    <t s="33">(Torah)</t>
    <t s="34">and repentance and good deeds are seemingly two different matters.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section elaborates that wisdom and repentance are not only different but opposites, as Torah study emphasizes the student's existence while repentance and good deeds emphasize self-nullification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And perhaps one could add,</t>
    <t s="2">that wisdom</t>
    <t s="3">(Torah)</t>
    <t s="4">and repentance and good deeds,</t>
    <t s="5">in addition to being different matters,</t>
    <t s="6">are also like opposites.</t>
    <t s="7">For in the study of Torah, the existence of the person engaged in Torah is emphasized,</t>
    <t s="8">for the mitzvah of Torah study is that one should understand and comprehend</t>
    <t s="9">(the subject being studied)</t>
    <t s="10">with one's own intellect.</t>
    <t s="11">To the extent that even regarding a legal ruling, one must rule specifically according to one's own understanding.</t>
    <t s="12">And as our Sages said,</t>
    <t s="13">"They differ in the Heavenly Academy... the Holy One, blessed be He, says... and the entire Heavenly Academy says...,"</t>
    <t s="14">the reason for this, that the Heavenly Academy ruled the law differently than the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="15">is,</t>
    <t s="16">because according to the rules of Torah, they must rule the law according to their understanding.</t>
    <t s="17">This matter applies even in the study of Torah in the Heavenly Academy.</t>
    <t s="18">And all the more so in the study of Torah of man below,</t>
    <t s="19">for "the Torah is not in heaven,"</t>
    <t s="20">and "the Holy One, blessed be He, laughs and says, 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me.'"</t>
    <t s="21">And in repentance and good deeds, the self-nullification of man is emphasized.</t>
    <t s="22">For the matter of repentance is that a person leaves and is nullified from his own existence,</t>
    <t s="23">"a sin-offering from here,"</t>
    <t s="24">and so it is regarding mitzvos</t>
    <t s="25">(good deeds),</t>
    <t s="26">for in addition to the fact that the fulfillment of mitzvos must be</t>
    <t s="27">(not from intellect,</t>
    <t s="28">but rather)</t>
    <t s="29">in the manner of the service of a servant,</t>
    <t s="30">the action that is accomplished through the fulfillment of mitzvos is that the limbs of the person fulfilling the mitzvah become a chariot for the Supernal Will,</t>
    <t s="31">and a chariot is a matter of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="32">And nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="33">the essence of Torah</t>
    <t s="34">(the purpose of wisdom)</t>
    <t s="35">(existence)</t>
    <t s="36">is repentance and good deeds</t>
    <t s="37">(self-nullification).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the opening header of the maamar, including the date and Torah portion.
This section explains the Gemara's statement that the purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, citing Rashi's interpretation that this refers to the essence of Torah.

translations.translation: "A saying that is regularly in the mouth of Rava: The purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, as it is said,
'The beginning of wisdom is fear of the L-rd; good understanding to all who do them,'
It does not say 'to those who study them,' but rather 'to those who do them.'
And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings this in his maamar beginning "Zeh she'amar" of Shabbos Parshas Vayishlach 5689
(printed in the Kuntres of Wedding Discourses 5689)
is that it should be accompanied by repentance and good deeds.
that the essence of Torah is understanding and comprehension,
that one should understand and comprehend what one studies
for when one does not understand what one studies, it is not considered study at all],
and in this statement of our Sages, it says that the essence of Torah is repentance and good deeds.
that the reason the maamar brings Rashi's commentary on "the purpose of wisdom,"
because the meaning of "purpose" in most places is the ultimate intention,
the meaning of "the purpose of wisdom is repentance and good deeds" is,
that the ultimate intention in the study of Torah
is that it should lead to repentance and good deeds.
Therefore the maamar brings Rashi's commentary that "the purpose of wisdom" is "the essence of Torah."
For in addition to the fact that the intention of Torah study is that it should lead to repentance and good deeds,
also the very essence of Torah itself
and repentance and good deeds are seemingly two different matters.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates that wisdom and repentance are not only different but opposites, as Torah study emphasizes the student's existence while repentance and good deeds emphasize self-nullification.

translations.translation: in addition to being different matters,
For in the study of Torah, the existence of the person engaged in Torah is emphasized,
for the mitzvah of Torah study is that one should understand and comprehend
To the extent that even regarding a legal ruling, one must rule specifically according to one's own understanding.
"They differ in the Heavenly Academy... the Holy One, blessed be He, says... and the entire Heavenly Academy says...,"
the reason for this, that the Heavenly Academy ruled the law differently than the Holy One, blessed be He,
because according to the rules of Torah, they must rule the law according to their understanding.
This matter applies even in the study of Torah in the Heavenly Academy.
And all the more so in the study of Torah of man below,
for "the Torah is not in heaven,"
and "the Holy One, blessed be He, laughs and says, 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me.'"
And in repentance and good deeds, the self-nullification of man is emphasized.
For the matter of repentance is that a person leaves and is nullified from his own existence,
and so it is regarding mitzvos
for in addition to the fact that the fulfillment of mitzvos must be
in the manner of the service of a servant,
the action that is accomplished through the fulfillment of mitzvos is that the limbs of the person fulfilling the mitzvah become a chariot for the Supernal Will,
and a chariot is a matter of self-nullification.
